verses.sanskrit:
भीष्म उवाच।
              एवं स्तुतः स भगवान् गुह्यैस्तथ्यैश्च नामभिः। तं मुनिं दर्शयामास नारदं विश्वरूपधृक्॥१॥
verses.english: Bhishma said Thus sung with names that were not known to others, the Divine Narayana having the universe for his form appeared before the ascetic Narada.

verses.sanskrit: किञ्चिच्चन्द्राद्विशुद्धात्मा किञ्चिच्चन्द्राद्विशेषवान्। कृशानुवर्णः किञ्चिच्च किञ्चिद्धिष्ण्याकृतिः प्रभुः॥२॥
verses.english: His form was some what purer than the moon and differed from the moon in some particulars. He somewhat resembled a burning fire in complexion. The powerful Lord was somewhat of the form of Vishti,

verses.sanskrit: शुकपत्रनिभः किञ्चित् किञ्चित्स्फटिकसन्निभः। नीलाञ्जनचयप्रख्यो जातरूपप्रभः क्वचित्॥३॥
verses.english: He looked in some respects like the feathers of the parrot, and in some a collection of pure crystal. He resembled in some respects a hill of antimony and in some a mass of pure gold.

verses.sanskrit: प्रवालाङ्कुरवर्णश्च श्वेतवर्णस्तथा क्वचित्। क्वचित्सुवर्णवर्णाभो वैदूर्यसदृशः क्वचित्॥४॥
verses.english: His complexion somewhat resembled the coral when first formed, and was somewhat white. That complexion resembled in some respects the colour of gold and in some that of the lapis lazulus.

verses.sanskrit: नीलवैदूर्यसदृश इन्द्रनीलनिभः क्वचित्। मयूरग्रीववर्णाभो मुक्ताहारनिभः क्वचित्॥५॥
verses.english: It resembled in some respects the colour of the blue lapis lazulus and in some that of sapphire. It resembled in some respects of colour of the peacock's neck, and in some that of a string of pearls.

verses.sanskrit: एतान्बहुविधान्वर्णान् रूपैर्बिभ्रत्सनातनः। सहस्रनयनः श्रीमाञ्छतशीर्षः सहस्रपात्॥६॥
verses.english: Bearing these various sorts of hues on his body the eternal Deity appeared before Narada. He had a thousand eyes and was endued with great beauty. He had a hundred heads and a hundred feet.

verses.sanskrit: सहस्रोदरबाहुश्च अव्यक्त इति च क्वचित्। ओङ्कारमुद्गिरन्वक्त्रात्सावित्रीं च तदन्वयाम्॥७॥
verses.english: He had a thousand stomachs and a thousand arms. He seemed to be still inconceivable to the mind. With one of his mouths he uttered the syllable OM and then the Gayatri following OM.

verses.sanskrit: शेषेभ्यश्चैव वक्त्रेभ्यश्चतुर्वेदान् गिरन्बहून्। आरण्यकं जगौ देवो हरिर्नारायणो वशी॥८॥
verses.english: With mind under complete mastery, the great God, called by the names of Hari and Narayana, by his other mouths, many in nụmber, uttered many Mantras from the four Vedas which are known by the name of Aranyaka.

verses.sanskrit: वेदिं कमण्डलुं शुभ्रान्मणीनुपानहौ कुशान्। अजिनं दण्डकाष्ठं च ज्वलितं च हुताशनम्॥९॥
verses.english: The Lord of all the gods, the great God who is worshipped in sacrifices, held in his hands a sacrificial altar, a Kamandalu, a few white gems, a pair of shoes, a bundle of Kusha blades, a deer-skin, a tooth-stick, and a little burning fire.

verses.sanskrit: धारयामास देवेशो हस्तैर्यज्ञपतिस्तदा। तं प्रसन्नं प्रसन्नात्मा नारदो द्विजसत्तमः॥१०॥
verses.english: With a cheerful heart, that foremost of twice-born one viz., Narada, controlling speech, bowed to the great God and worshipped Him.

verses.sanskrit: वाग्यतः प्रणतो भूत्वा ववन्दे परमेश्वरम्। तमुवाच नतं मूर्ध्ना देवानामादिरव्ययः॥११॥
verses.english: The first of all the gods, who is free from decay, said the following words to him whose head was still bent low in veneration.

verses.sanskrit: श्रीभगवानुवाच । एकतश्च द्वितश्चैव त्रितश्चैव महर्षयः। इमं देशमनुप्राप्ता मम दर्शनलालसाः॥१२॥
verses.english: The Holy One said The great Rishis, Ekata, Dvita, and Trita, came to this country from desire of seeing me.

verses.sanskrit: न च मां ते ददृशिरे न च द्रक्ष्यति कश्चन। ऋते ह्यैकान्तिकश्रेष्ठात्त्वं चैवैकान्तिकोत्तम॥१३॥
verses.english: Their wishes, however, were not fulfilled. Excepting those who are devoted to with wholly and solely, no else can see me. As regards you, you are verily the foremost of all persons devoted to me with all their souls.

verses.sanskrit: ममैतास्तनवः श्रेष्ठा जाता धर्मगृहे द्विज। तास्त्वं भजस्व सततं साधयस्व यथागतम्॥१४॥
verses.english: These are my bodies, the best ones that I assume. These were born, O twice-born one, in the house of Dharma. Do you worship them always, and do you perform those rites that are laid down in the ordinances in connexion with that worship.

verses.sanskrit: वृणीष्व च वरं विप्र मत्तस्त्वं यदिहेच्छसि। प्रसन्नोऽहं तवाद्येह विश्वमूर्तिरिहाव्ययः॥१५॥
verses.english: O Brahmana, do you ask of me the boons you wish! I am pleased with you to-day and I appear to you now in my universal form as freed from decay and deterioration!

verses.sanskrit:
नारद उवाच।
              अद्य मे तपसो देव यमस्य नियमस्य च। सद्यः फलमवाप्तं वै दृष्टो यद्भगवान्मया॥१६॥
verses.english: Narada said Since, O holy one, I have to-day succeeded in seeing you, I think that I have acquired forthwith the fruits of my penances, O God, of my self-restraint, and of all the vows and observances that I have practised.

verses.sanskrit: वर एष ममात्यन्तं दृष्टस्त्वं यत्सनातनः। भगवन्विश्वदृक् सिंहः सर्वमूर्तिर्महान्प्रभुः॥१७॥
verses.english: This, indeed, is the highest boon you have granted me for you have appeared before me to-day, O Eternal Lord! You, O holy one, have the universe for your eye! You are the Lion. Your form is identifiable with everything! Possessed of power you, O Lord, are vast and infinite.

verses.sanskrit:
भीष्म उवाच।
              एवं संदर्शयित्वा तु नारदं परमेष्ठिनम्। उवाच वचनं भूयो गच्छ नारद मा चिरम्॥१८॥
verses.english: Bhishma said Having thus appeared before Narada the son of Parameshthi, the great God addressed that ascetic and said,-Go hence, O Narada, and do not delay!

verses.sanskrit: इमे ह्यनिन्द्रियाहारा मद्भक्ताश्चन्द्रवर्चसः। एकाग्राश्चिन्तयेयुर्मां नैषां विघ्नो भवेदिति॥१९॥
verses.english: These worshippers of mine, having moonlike complexions, are divested of all senses and do not live upon any kind of food. They are, again, all Liberated! With minds wholly concentrated upon me, people should think of me. Such worshippers will never meet with any obstacles.

verses.sanskrit: सिद्धा ह्येते महाभागाः पुरा ह्येकान्तिनोऽभवन्। तमोरजोभिर्निर्मुक्ता मां प्रवेक्ष्यन्त्यसंशयम्॥२०॥
verses.english: These men have all acquired ascetic success and are highly blessed. In day of yore they became entirely devoted to me. They have becn freed from the qualities of Darkness and Ignorance. Forsooth, they are competent to enter me and become merged into my Self.

verses.sanskrit: न दृश्यश्चक्षुषा योऽसौ न स्पृश्यः स्पर्शनेन च। न घ्रेयश्चैव गन्धेन रसेन च विवर्जितः॥२१॥
verses.english: He who cannot be seen with the eye, touched with the sense of touch, smelt with the sense of scent, and who is beyond the sense of taste, He whom the three qualities of goodness. Darkness, and Ignorance do not touch, who permeates all things and is the one Witness of the universe, and who is described as the Soul of the entire universe, He who is not destroyed upon the destruction of the bodies of all created things, who is unborn and unchangeable and eternal, who is freed from all qualities, who is indivisible and entire, He who is above the twenty-four topics of enquiry and is considered the Twenty-fifth, who is called by the name of Twenty-fifth, who is called by the name of Purusha, who is inactive, and who is said to be apprehended by Knowledge alone, He into whom the foremost of twice-born ones enter and become liberated, He is the eternal Supreme Soul and is known by the name of Vasudeva.

verses.sanskrit: सत्त्वं रजस्तमश्चैव न गुणास्तं भजन्ति वै। यश्च सर्वगतः साक्षी लोकस्यात्मेति कथ्यते॥२२॥
भूतग्रामशरीरेषु नश्यत्सु न विनश्यति। अजो नित्यः शाश्वतश्च निर्गुणो निष्कलस्तथा॥२३॥
द्विर्द्वादशेभ्यस्तत्त्वेभ्यः ख्यातो यः पञ्चविंशकः। पुरुषो निष्क्रियश्चैव ज्ञानदृश्यश्च कथ्यते॥२४॥
यं प्रविश्य भवन्तीह मुक्ता वै द्विजसत्तमाः। स वासुदेवो विज्ञेयः परमात्मा सनातनः॥२५॥
पश्य देवस्य माहात्म्यं महिमानं च नारद। शुभाशुभैः कर्मभिर्यो न लिप्यति कदाचन॥२६॥
verses.english: See, O Narada, the greatness and power of that God! He is never affected by good or bad deeds.

verses.sanskrit: सत्त्वं रजस्तमश्चेति गुणानेतान्प्रचक्षते। यत्ते सर्वशरीरेषु तिष्ठन्ति विचरन्ति च॥२७॥
verses.english: Satvata, Rajas, and Tamas, are said to be the three (original) qualities. These live and act in the bodies of all creatures.

verses.sanskrit: एतान्गुणांस्तु क्षेत्रज्ञो भुङ्क्ते नैभिः स भुज्यते। निर्गुणो गुणभुक्चैव गुणस्रष्टा गुणाधिकः॥२८॥
verses.english: The Individual Soul, called Kshetrajna, enjoys and suffers the action of these three qualities. He, however, is above them and they cannot touch Him. Freed from these qualities, He is again their enjoyer and sufferer. Having created them Himself, He is above them all.

verses.sanskrit: जगत्प्रतिष्ठा देवर्षे पृथिव्यप्सु प्रलीयते। ज्योतिष्यापः प्रलीयन्ते ज्योतिर्वायौ प्रलीयते॥२९॥
verses.english: O celestial Rishi, the Earth, which is the refuge of the universe, disappears into water. Water disappears into Fire and Fire into Wind. Wind disappears into Ether, and Ether into Mind. Mind is a great creature, and it disappears into Unmanifest Nature.

verses.sanskrit: खे वायुः प्रलयं याति मनस्याकाशमेव च। मनो हि परमं भूतं तदव्यक्ते प्रलीयते॥३०॥
अव्यक्तं पुरुषे ब्रह्मन्निष्क्रिये संप्रलीयते। नास्ति तस्मात्परतरः पुरुषाद्वै सनातनात्॥३१॥
verses.english: Unmanifest Nature, 0 Brahmana, disappears into Inactive Purusha (Soul). There is nothing higher than Purusha (Soul) which is Eternal.

verses.sanskrit: नित्यं हि नास्ति जगति भूतं स्थावरजङ्गमम्। ऋते तमेकं पुरुषं वासुदेवं सनातनम्॥३२॥
verses.english: There is nothing among mobile and immobile things in the universe which is immutable, except Vasudeva, the eternal Purusha.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वभूतात्मभूतो हि वासुदेवो महाबलः। पृथिवी वायुराकाशमापो ज्योतिश्च पञ्चमम्॥३३॥
ते समेता महात्मानः शरीरमिति संज्ञितम्। तदा विशति यो ब्रह्मन्नदृश्यो लघुविक्रमः॥३४॥
verses.english: Endued with great power, Vasudeva is the Soul of all creatures. Earth, Wind, Ether, Water, and Fire forming fifth, are primal clephants of great power. Mingling together they form the body. Possessed of subtile prowess and invisible to all eyes, O Brahmana, the powerful Vasudeva then enter that combination of the five principal elements called body. Such entrance is called his birth, and taking birth He makes the body move about and act. Without a combination of the five principal elements, 110 body can ever be formed.

verses.sanskrit: उत्पन्न एव भवति शरीरं चेष्टयन्प्रभुः। न विना धातुसंघातं शरीरं भवति क्वचित्॥३५॥
न च जीवं विना ब्रह्मन्वायवश्चेष्टयन्त्युत। स जीवः परिसंख्यातः शेषः संकर्षणः प्रभुः॥३६॥
verses.english: Without, again, the entrance of Individual Soul into the body, the mind living within it cannot cause it move and act. He that enters the body is possessed of great power and is called Individual. He is known also by other names, viz., Shesha and Sankarshana.

verses.sanskrit: तस्मात्सनत्कुमारत्वं योऽलभत्स्वेन कर्मणा। यस्मिंश्च सर्वभूतानि प्रलयं यान्ति संक्षयम्॥३७॥
verses.english: He who takes his his rise, from that Sankarshana, by his own acts, Sanatkumara, and in whom all creatures merge when the universal dissolution sets in, is the Mind of all creatures and is called by the name of Praddyumna.

verses.sanskrit: स मनः सर्वभूतानां प्रद्युम्नः परिपठ्यते। तस्मात्प्रसूतो यः कर्ता कारणं कार्यमेव च॥३८॥
verses.english: From Him originates. He who is the Creator, and who is both Cause and Effect. From this last, everything, viz., the mobile and immobile universe, originates. This one is called Aniruddha. He is otherwise called Ishana and He is manifest in all deeds.

verses.sanskrit: तस्मात्सर्वं संभवति जगत्स्थावरजङ्गमम्। सोऽनिरुद्धः स ईशानो व्यक्तः स सर्वकर्मसु॥३९॥
यो वासुदेवो भगवान्क्षेत्रज्ञो निर्गुणात्मकः। ज्ञेयः स एव राजेन्द्र जीव: संकर्षणः प्रभुः॥४०॥
verses.english: That illustrious one, viz., Vasudeva, who is called Kshetrajna, (Soul) and who is freed from qualities, should, O king of kings, be known as the powerful Sankarshana, when He takes birth as (Individual Soul).

verses.sanskrit: संकर्षणाच्च प्रद्युम्नो मनोभूतः स उच्यते। प्रद्युम्नाद्योऽनिरुद्धस्तु सोऽहंकारः स ईश्वरः॥४१॥
verses.english: From Sankarshana originates Praddyumna who is called “Mind-begotten." From Praddymuna is He who is Aniruddha. He is Consciousness, He is Ishvara (Supreme Lord).

verses.sanskrit: मत्तः सर्वं संभवति जगत्स्थावरजङ्गमम्। अक्षरं च क्षरं चैव सच्चासच्चैव नारद॥४२॥
verses.english: It is from me that the entire mobile and immobile universe originates. It is from me, O Narada, that the indestructible and the destructible, the existent and the non-existent, originates.

verses.sanskrit: मां प्रविश्य भवन्तीह मुक्ता भक्तास्तु ये मम। अहं हि पुरुषो ज्ञेयो निष्क्रियः पञ्चविंशकः॥४३॥
verses.english: They who are devoted to me enter into me and become liberated. I am known as Purusha. Without acts, I am the Twenty-fifth.

verses.sanskrit: निर्गुणो निष्कलश्चैव निर्द्वन्द्वो निष्परिग्रहः। एतत्त्वया न विज्ञेयं रूपवानिति दृश्यते॥४४॥
verses.english: Getting over qualities, I am entire and indivisible. I am above all pairs of opposite and shorn of all attachments. This, O Narada, you will fail to understand. You see me as having a form. If I wish, I can dissolve this form in a moment. I am the Supreme Lord and the Preceptor of the universe.

verses.sanskrit: इच्छन्मुहूर्तान्नश्येयमीशोऽहं जगतो गुरुः। माया ह्येषा मया सृष्टा यन्मां पश्यसि नारद॥४५॥
verses.english: What you see of me, ONarada, is merely an illusion of mine. I now appear to be possessed of the attributes of all created things. You are not competent to know me. I have shown to you duly my fourfold form. I am, O Narada, the doer, I am Cause, and I am Effect.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वभूतगुणैर्युक्तं नैव त्वं ज्ञातुमर्हसि। मयैतत्कथितं सम्यक्तव मूर्तिचतुष्टयम्॥४६॥
अहं हि जीवसंज्ञातो मयि जीवः समाहितः। नैवं ते बुद्धिरत्राभूदॄष्टो जीवो मयेति वै॥४७॥
verses.english: I am the sum-total of all living creatures. All living creatures have their refuge in me, Do not think that you have seen the Individual Soul.

verses.sanskrit: अहं सर्वत्रगो ब्रह्मन्भूतग्रामान्तरात्मकः। भूतग्रामशरीरेषु नश्यत्सु न नशाम्यहम्॥४८॥
verses.english: I pervade all things, O Brahmana, and am the inner Soul of all creatures. When the bodies of all creatures, however, are destroyed, I am not destroyed.

verses.sanskrit: सिद्धा हि ते महाभागा नरा ह्येकान्तिनोऽभवन्। तमोरजोभ्यां निर्मुक्ताः प्रवेक्ष्यन्ति च मां मुने॥४९॥
verses.english: Those highly blessed men who, having acquired ascetic success, become entirely devoted to me, become freed from the qualities of both Darkness and Ignorance and succeed, therefore, in entering me, O great ascetic.

verses.sanskrit: हिरण्यगर्भो लोकादिश्चतुर्वक्त्रोऽनिरुक्तगः। ब्रह्मा सनातनो देवो मम बह्वर्थचिन्तकः॥५०॥
verses.english: He called Hiranyagarbha, who is the beginning of the world, who has four faces, who cannot be understood with the help of the Nirukta, who is otherwise called Brahman, who is an eternal god, is engaged in loO king after many of my works.

verses.sanskrit: ललाटाच्चैव मे रुद्रो देवः क्रोधाद्विनिःसृतः। पश्यैकादश मे रुद्रान्दक्षिणं पार्श्वमास्थितान्॥५१॥
verses.english: The god Rudra, born of my anger, originated from my forehead. See, the eleven Rudras are increasing on the right side of my person.

verses.sanskrit: द्वादशैव तथाऽऽदित्यान् वामपार्श्वे समास्थितान्। अग्रतश्चैव मे पश्य वसूनष्टौ सुरोत्तमान्॥५२॥
verses.english: The twelve Adityas are on the left side of my person. See the eight Vasus, those foremnost of gods, are in my front, and see, Nasatya and Dasra, those two celestial physicians, are in the rear. See also in my body all the Prajapatis and see the seven Rishis Also.

verses.sanskrit: नासत्यं चैव दस्रं च भिषजौ पश्य पृष्ठतः। सर्वान्प्रजापतीन्पश्य पश्य सप्त ऋषींस्तथा॥५३॥
वेदान्यज्ञांश्च शतशः पश्यामृतमथौषधीः। तपांसि नियमांश्चैव यमानपि पृथग्विधान्॥५४॥
verses.english: See also the Vedas, all the Sacrifices numbering by hundreds, the Amrita (nectar), and all the (medicinal) herbs and plants, and Penances, and vows and observances of various sorts.

verses.sanskrit: तथाऽष्टगुणमैश्वर्यमेकस्थं पश्य मूर्तिमत्। श्रियं लक्ष्मीं च कीर्तिं च पृथिवीं च ककुद्मिनीम्॥५५॥
verses.english: See also in me the eight attributes of power, viz., those particularly called the Lordly powers, living all together in my body in their united and embodied form. See also Shree and Lakshmi, and Kirti, and the Earth with her hump.

verses.sanskrit: वेदानां मातरं पश्य मत्स्थां देवीं सरस्वतीम्। ध्रुवं च ज्योतिषां श्रेष्ठ पश्य नारद खेचरम्॥५६॥
verses.english: See the goddess Sarasvati, that mother of the Vedas, living in me! See, O Narada, Dhruva, that foremost of luminaries ranging in the sky.

verses.sanskrit: अंभोधरान्समुद्रांश्च सरांसि सरितस्तथा। मूर्तिमन्तः पितृगणांश्चतुरः पश्य सत्तम॥५७॥
verses.english: See also all the Oceans, those receptacles of water, and lakes, and rivers. See, also, O best of men, the four foremost ones amongst the Pitris in their embodied forms. See also, living in me, the three qualities (of Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas) which are formless.

verses.sanskrit: त्रींश्चैवेमान्गुणान्पश्य मत्स्थान्मूर्तिविवर्जितान्। देवकार्यादपि मुने पितृकार्यं विशिष्यते॥५८॥
देवानां च पितॄणां च पिता ह्येकोऽहमादितः। अहं हयशिरा भूत्वा समुद्रे पश्चिमोत्तरे॥५९॥
verses.english: The acts done in honour of the departed mane are superior to those done in honour of the gods. I am the Pitri of the both the gods and the Pitris, and am existing from the beginning.

verses.sanskrit: पिबामि सुहुतं हव्यं कव्यं च श्रद्धयाऽन्वितम्। मया सृष्टः पुरा ब्रह्मा मां यज्ञमयजत्स्वयम्॥६०॥
verses.english: Becoming the Equine-head I pass through the Western and the Northern ocean and drink sacrificial libations duly poured with Mantras and solid sacrificial food offered with respect and devotion.

verses.sanskrit: ततस्तस्मिन्वरान्प्रीतो दत्त्वानसम्यनुत्तमान्। मत्पुत्रत्वं च कल्पादौ लोकाध्यक्षत्वमेव च॥६१॥
verses.english: In ancient times I created Brahman who himself worshipped me in sacrifices. Pleased with him on that account I granted him many excellent boons.

verses.sanskrit: अहंकारकृतं चैव नाम पर्यायवाचकम्। त्वया कृतां च मर्यादा नातिक्रंस्यति कश्चन॥६२॥
verses.english: I said to him that in the beginning of the cycle he would be born to me as my son, and the sovereignty of all the worlds would he enjoy, and various names will be given to diverse objects on account of the Ahankara, i. e., egoism, coming into existence.

verses.sanskrit: त्वं चैव वरदो ब्रह्मन्वरेप्सूनां भविष्यसि। सुरासुरगणानां च ऋषीणां च तपोधन॥६३॥
verses.english: I also told him that none would ever violate the limits and boundaries he would lay down, and, further that he would be the giver of boons to persons who would solicit him for the same.

verses.sanskrit: पितॄणां च महाभाग सततं संशितव्रत। विविधानां च भूतानां त्वमुपास्यो भविष्यसि॥६४॥
verses.english: I further assured him that he would be an object of worship with all the gods and Asuras, all the Rishis and Pitris, and the various creatures forming the creation.

verses.sanskrit: प्रादुर्भावगतश्चाहं सुरकार्येषु नित्यदा। अनुशास्यस्त्वया ब्रह्मन्नियोज्यश्च सुतो यथा॥६५॥
verses.english: I also gave him to understand that I would always appear for performing the business of the gods and for that I would allow myself to be commanded by him even as a son by his father.

verses.sanskrit: एतांश्चान्यांश्च रुचिरान्ब्रह्मणेऽमिततेजसे। अहं दत्त्वा वरान्प्रीतो निवृत्तिपरमोऽभवम्॥६६॥
verses.english: Granting these and other highly agreeable boons to Brahman of great energy on account of my being propitiated with him I adopted the course dictated by Renunciation.

verses.sanskrit: निर्वाणं सर्वधर्माणां निवृत्तिः परमा स्मृता। तस्मान्निवृत्तिमापन्नश्चरेत्सर्वाङ्गनिर्वृतः॥६७॥
verses.english: The highest Renunciation is the annihilation of all duties and acts. Hence, by adopting Renunciation one should act in complete happiness.

verses.sanskrit: विद्यासहायवन्तं च आदित्यस्थं समाहितम्। कपिलं प्राहुराचार्याः सांख्यनिश्चितनिश्चयाः॥६८॥
verses.english: Learned preceptors, with settled conclusions deducted from the truths of the Sankhya philosophy, have spoken of me as Kapila endued with the power of knowledge, living within the effulgence of the Sun, and concentrated in Yoga.

verses.sanskrit: हिरण्यगर्भो भगवानेष च्छन्दसि सुष्टुतः। सोऽहं योगरतिर्ब्रह्मन्योगशास्त्रेषु शब्दितः॥६९॥
verses.english: In the Vedas I have been repeatedly hymned as the illustrious Hiranyagarbha. In the Yoga-Shastras, O Brahmana, I have been spoken of as one who find pleasure in Yoga.

verses.sanskrit: एषोऽहं व्यक्तिमागत्य तिष्ठामि दिवि शाश्वतः। ततो युगसहस्रान्ते संहरिष्ये जगत्पुनः॥७०॥
verses.english: I am eternal. Assuming a form that is manifest, I live at present, in the sky. At the end of a thousand cycles, I shall once more withdraw the universe into myself.

verses.sanskrit: कृत्वाऽऽत्मस्थानि भूतानि स्थावराणि चराणि च। एकाकी विद्यया सार्धं विहरिष्ये जगत्पुनः॥७१॥
verses.english: Having withdrawn all creatures, mobile and immobile, into myself, I shall exist all alone with Knowledge only as my companion.

verses.sanskrit: ततो भूयो जगत्सर्वं करिष्यामीह विद्यया। अस्मिन्मूर्तिश्चतुर्थी या साऽसृजज्छेषमव्ययम्॥७२॥
verses.english: After the lapse of ages I shall again create the universe, with the help of that Knowledge. My fourth form creates the indestructible Shesha.

verses.sanskrit: स हि संकर्षणः प्रोक्तः प्रद्युम्नं सोऽप्यजीजनत्। प्रद्युम्नादनिरुद्धोऽहं सर्गो मम पुनः पुनः॥७३॥
verses.english: That Shesha is called by the name of Sankarshana. Sankarshana creates Praddyumna. From Praddyumna I take birth myself as Aniruddha. I Aniruddha. I create (myself) repeatedly.

verses.sanskrit: अनिरुद्धात्तथा ब्रह्मा तन्नाभिकमलोद्भवः। ब्रह्मणः सर्वभूतानि चराणि स्थावराणि च॥७४॥
verses.english: From Aniruddha originates Brahman. The latter is born from Aniruddha's navel. From Brahman originate all mobile and immobile creatures.

verses.sanskrit: एतां सृष्टिं विजानीहि कल्पादिषु पुनः पुनः। यथा सूर्यस्य गगनादुदयास्तमने इह॥७५॥
verses.english: Know that Creation originates in this way repeatedly at the beginning of every cycle. Creation and destruction succeed each other like sunrise and sunset in this world.

verses.sanskrit: नष्टे पुनर्बलात्काल आनयत्यमितद्युतिः। तथा बलादहं पृथ्वीं सर्वभूतहिताय वै॥७६॥
verses.english: Then, again, as Time, gifted with great energy, forcibly brings back the Sun after his disappearance, similarly I shall, assuming the form of a boar and displaying my strength, bring back the Earth with her belt of seas to her own position for the behoof of all creatures when she becomes submerged in water. I shall then kill the son of Diti, named Hiranyagarbha, elated with pride of strength.

verses.sanskrit: सत्त्वैराक्रान्तसर्वाङ्गां नष्टां सागरमेखलाम्। आनयिष्यामि स्वस्थानं वाराहं रूपमास्थितः॥७७॥
हिरण्याक्षं वधिष्यामि दैतेयं बलगर्वितम्। नारसिंहं वपुः कृत्वा हिरण्यकशिपुं पुनः॥७८॥
सुरकार्ये हनिष्यामि यज्ञघ्नं दितिनन्दनम्। विरोचनस्य बलवान्बलिः पुत्रो महासुरः॥७९॥
verses.english: Assuming the form then of a Manlion, I shall, for doing good to the gods, kill Hiranyakasipu, the son of Diti, who will be a great destroyer of sacrifices.

verses.sanskrit: अवध्यः सर्वलोकानां सदेवासुररक्षसाम्। भविष्यति स शक्रं वा स्वराज्याच्च्यावयिष्यति॥८०॥
verses.english: Virochana will have a powerful son named Vali. The entire universe consisting of gods, Asuras, and Rakshasas will not be able to kill that great Asura. He will hurl Shakra from the sovereignty of the universe.

verses.sanskrit: त्रैलोक्येऽपहृते तेन विमुखे च शचीपतौ। अदित्यां द्वादशादित्यः संभविष्यामि कश्यपात्॥८१॥
verses.english: When after defeating the Lord of Shachi, that Asura will possess the sovereignty of the three worlds, I shall take birth in Aditi's womb, by Kashyapa, as the twelfth Aditya.

verses.sanskrit: ततो राज्यं प्रदास्यामि शक्रायामिततेजसे। देवताः स्थापयिष्यामि स्वस्वस्थानेषु नारद॥८२॥
verses.english: I shall restore it to Indra of immeasurable splendour, and replace the gods, O Narada, in their respective stations,

verses.sanskrit: बलिं चैव करिष्यामि पातालतलवासिनम्। दानवं च बलिश्रेष्ठमवध्यं सर्वदैवतैः॥८३॥
verses.english: As regards Vali, that foremost of Danavas, who is to be unslayable by all the gods, I shall cause him to live in the nether regions.

verses.sanskrit: त्रेतायुगे भविष्यामि रामो भृगुकुलोद्वहः। क्षत्रं चोत्सादयिष्यामि समृद्धबलवाहनम्॥८४॥
verses.english: In the Treta age I shall take birth as Rama in the race of Bhrigu, and root out the Kshatriyas who will become proud of their strength and riches.

verses.sanskrit: संध्यांशे समनुप्राप्ते त्रेताया द्वापरस्य च। अहं दाशरथी रामो भविष्यामि जगत्पतिः॥८५॥
verses.english: Towards the end of Treta and the beginning of Dvapara, I shall take birth as Rama the son of Dasharatha in Ikshvaku's race.

verses.sanskrit: त्रितोपघाताद्वैरूप्यमेकतोऽथ द्वितस्तथा। प्राप्स्येते वानरत्वं हि प्रजापतिसुतावृषी॥८६॥
verses.english: At that time, the two Rishis, viz., the two sons of Prajapati, called by the names of Ekata and Dvita, will on account of the injury done by them to their brother Trita, have to take birth as monkeys, losing the beauty of the human forin.

verses.sanskrit: तयोर्ये त्वन्वये जाता भविष्यन्ति वनौकसः। महाबला महावीर्याः शक्रतुल्यपराक्रमाः॥८७॥
verses.english: Those monkeys that shall take birth in the race of Ekata and Dvita, shall become endued with great power and mighty energy and will equal Shakra himself in power. All those monkeys, O twice-born one, will become my allies for performing the work of the gods.

verses.sanskrit: ते सहाया भविष्यन्ति सुरकार्ये मम द्विज। ततो रक्षःपतिं घोरं पुलस्त्यकुलपांसनम्॥८८॥
हरिष्ये रावणं रौद्रं सगणं लोककण्टकम्। द्वापरस्य कलेश्चैव सन्धौ पार्यवसानिके॥८९॥
verses.english: I shall then kill the dreadful king of the Rakshasas, that wretch of Pulastya's race, viz., the fierce Ravana, that thorn of all worlds, together with all his children and followers.

verses.sanskrit: प्रादुर्भाव: कंसहेतोर्मथुरायां भविष्यति। तत्राहं दानवान्हत्वा सुबहून् देवकण्टकान्॥९०॥
verses.english: At the junction the Dvapara and the Kali ages, I shall again appear in the world taking birth in city of Mathura for the purpose of killing Kansa.

verses.sanskrit: कुशस्थलीं करिष्यामि निवेशं द्वारकां पुरीम्। वसानस्तत्र वै पुर्यामदितेर्विप्रियंकरम्॥९१॥
verses.english: There, after killing numberless Danavas that will be as thorns in the side of the gods, I shali take up my residence in Kushasthali at the city of Dwaraka.

verses.sanskrit: हनिष्ये नरकं भौमं मुरं पीठं च दानवम्। प्राग्ज्योतिषं पुरं रम्यं नानाधनसमन्वितम्॥९२॥
verses.english: While living in that city I shall kill the Asura Naraka the chief of the Earth,-him, that is, who will do an injury to Aditi, as also some other Danavas of the names of Muru and Pitha.

verses.sanskrit: कुशस्थलीं नयिष्यामि हत्वा वै दानवोत्तमम्। महेश्वरमहासेनौ बाणप्रियहितैषिणौ॥९३॥
verses.english: Killing also another foremost of Danavas, viz., the kill of Pragjyotisha, I shall transplant that delightful city furnished with various kinds of wealth into Dwaraka.

verses.sanskrit: पराजेष्याम्यथोद्युक्तौ देवौ लोकनमस्कृतौ। ततः सुतं बलेर्जित्वा बाणं बाहुसहस्रिणम्॥९४॥
verses.english: I shall then defeat the two gods adored of all the deities, viz., Maheshvara and Mahasena, who will become fond of the Danava Vana and do him various good offices and who will try their best for that worshipper of theirs.

verses.sanskrit: विनाशयिष्यामि ततः सर्वान्सौभनिवासिनः। यः कालयवनः ख्यातो गर्गतेजोऽभिसंवृतः॥९५॥
verses.english: Defeating next the son of the Danava Vali, viz., Bana, who will be possessed a thousandarms, I shall next destroy all the inhabitants of the Danava city called Saubha.

verses.sanskrit: भविष्यति वधस्तस्य मत्त एव द्विजोत्तम। जरासन्धश्च बलवान्सर्वराजविरोधनः॥९६॥
verses.english: I shall next, O foremost of Brahmanas, bring about the death of Kalayavana, a Danava who will be endued with great power on account of his being equipt with the energy of Gargya.

verses.sanskrit: भविष्यत्यसुरः स्फीतो भूमिपालो गिरिव्रजे। मम बुद्धिपरिस्पन्दाद्वधस्तस्य भविष्यति॥९७॥
verses.english: A proud Asura will appear as a king at Girivraja, of the name of Jarasandha, who will fall out with all the other kings of the world. His death will be brought about by me through some one else guided by my intelligence.

verses.sanskrit: शिशुपालं वधिष्यामि यज्ञे धर्मसुतस्य वै। समागतेषु बलिषु पृथिव्यां सर्वराजसु॥९८॥
verses.english: I shall next kill Shisupala in the sacrifice of king Yudhishthira the son of Dharma, into which sacrifice all the kings of the world will bring tribute. In some of these works, only Arjuna, the son of Vasava, will become my assistant.

verses.sanskrit: वासविः सुसहायो वै मम त्वेको भविष्यति। युधिष्ठिरं स्थापयिष्ये स्वराज्ये भ्रातृभिः सह॥९९॥
एवं लोका वदिष्यन्ति नरनारायणावृषी। उद्युक्तौ दहतः क्षत्रं लोककार्यार्थमीश्वरौ॥१००॥
verses.english: I shall place Yudhishthira with all his brothers in his ancestral kingdom. People will call me and Arjuna as Narayana and Nara, when, endued with power, we two, putting forth our strength, shall kill a large number of Kshatriyas, for doing good to the world. Having lightened the load of the Earth according to our pleasure, I shall merge all the principal Satvatas, as also Dwaraka, my favourite city, into my own self, recollecting my all-einbracing Knowledge.

verses.sanskrit: कृत्वा भारावतरणं वसुधाया यथेप्सितम्। सर्वसात्वतमुख्यानां द्वारकायाश्च सत्तम॥१०१॥
करिष्ये प्रलयं घोरमात्मज्ञानाभिसंहितः। कर्माण्यपरिमेयाणि चतुर्मूर्तिधरो ह्यहम्॥१०२॥
कृत्वा लोकान्गमिष्यामि स्वानहं ब्रह्मसत्कृतान्। हंस: कूर्मश्च मत्स्यश्च प्रादुर्भावाद्द्विजोत्तम॥१०३॥
verses.english: Having four forms, I shall, in this way, perform many feats of great prowess, and attain at last to those regions of happiness created by me and honoured by all the Brahmanas.

verses.sanskrit: वराहो नरसिंहश्च वामनो राम एव च। रामो दाशरथिश्चैव सात्वतः कल्किरेव च॥१०४॥
verses.english: Appearing in the forms of a swan, a tortoise, a fish, O foremost of twice-born ones, I shall then appear as a boar, then as a manlion, then as a dwarf, then as Rama of Bhrigu's race, then as Rama the son of Dasharatha, then as Krishna the scion of the Satvata race, and lastly as Kalki.

verses.sanskrit: यदा वेदश्रुतिर्नष्टा मया प्रत्याहृता पुनः। सवेदाः सश्रुतीकाश्च कृताः पूर्वं कृते युगे॥१०५॥
verses.english: When the Vedas disappeared from the world, I brought them back. The Vedas, were re-created by me in the Krita age.

verses.sanskrit: अतिक्रान्ताः पुराणेषु श्रुतास्ते यदि वा क्वचित्। अतिक्रान्ताश्च बहवः प्रादुर्भावा ममोत्तमाः॥१०६॥
verses.english: They have once more disappeared or may only be partially heard here and there in the Puranas. Many of my best incarnations also in the world have become facts of the past.

verses.sanskrit: लोककार्याणि कृत्वा च पुनः स्वां प्रकृतिं गताः। न ह्येतद्ब्रह्मणा प्राप्तमीदृशं मम दर्शनम्॥१०७॥
verses.english: Having secured the good of the worlds in those forms in which I appeared, they have reentered into my own Nature. Brahman (the Creator) himself never saw me in this form of mine, which you, O Narada, have seen to-day on account of your entire devotion to me. I have now said to you, who are devoted to me wholly, everything, O Brahmana. . I have described to you my ancient appearances and future ones also, O best of inen, together with ail their mysteries.

verses.sanskrit: यत्त्वया प्राप्तमद्येह एकान्तगतबुद्धिना। एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं ब्रह्मन्भक्तिमतो मया॥१०८॥

पुराणं च भविष्यं च सरहस्यं च सत्तम।
              भीष्म उवाच।
              एवं स भगवान्देवो विश्वमूर्तिधरोऽव्ययः॥१०९॥
एतावदुक्त्वा वचनं तत्रैवान्तर्दधे पुनः। नारदोऽपि महातेजाः प्राप्यानुग्रहमीप्सितम्॥११०॥
नरनारायणौ द्रष्टुं बदर्याश्रममाद्रवत्। इदं महोपनिषदं चतुर्वेदसमन्वितम्॥१११॥
verses.english: Having won the high favour that he had solicited, Narada also, gifted with great energy, then proceeded in all haste to the retreat called Vadari, for seeing Nara and Narayana.

verses.sanskrit: सांख्ययोगकृतं तेन पञ्चरात्रानुशब्दितम्। नारायणमुखोद्गीतं नारदोऽश्रावयत्पुनः॥११२॥
verses.english: This great Upanishad quite of a piece with the four Vedas, and the Sankhya-Yoga, and called by him by the name of the Pancharatra Scriptures and recited by Narayana himself with his own mouth, was repeated by Narada before a large audience in the residence of Brahman (his sire) in exactly the same way in which Narayana had recited it and in which he had heard it from his own lips."

verses.sanskrit:
ब्रह्मणः सदने तात यथा दृष्टं यथा श्रुतम्।
              युधिष्ठिर उवाच।
              एतदाश्चर्यभूतं हि माहात्म्यं तस्य धीमतः॥११३॥
किं वै ब्रह्मा न जानीते यतः शुश्राव नारदात्। पितामहोऽपि भगवांस्तस्माद्देवादनन्तरः॥११४॥
verses.english: Yudhishthira said “Was not Brahman. the Creator of all things, acquainted with this wonderful discourse of the glory of Narayana gifted with intelligence that he heard it from the lips of Narada?

verses.sanskrit:
कथं स न विजानीयात्प्रभावममितौजसः।
              भीष्म उवाच।
              महाकल्पसहस्राणि महाकल्पशतानि च॥११५॥
verses.english: Is the illustrious Grandfather of all the worlds any way different from or inferior to the great Narayana? How then it is that he was unacquainted with the power of Narayana of great energy?"

verses.sanskrit: समतीतानि राजेन्द्र सर्गाश्च प्रलयाश्च ह। सर्गस्यादौ स्मृतो ब्रह्मा प्रजासर्गकरः प्रभुः॥११६॥
verses.english: Bhishma continued "Hundreds and thousands of great cycles, hundreds and thousands of Creations and Dissolutions, O king of kings, have been over and become events of the past.

verses.sanskrit: जानाति देवप्रवरं भूयश्चातोऽधिकं नृप। परमात्मानमीशानमात्मनः प्रभवं तथा॥११७॥
verses.english: In the beginning of every Creation, Brahman, endued with great power and who creates all things, is remembered by Narayana). Brahman knows well, O king, that Narayana, that foremost of all gods is very much superior to him.

verses.sanskrit: ये त्वन्ये ब्रह्मसदने सिद्धसंघाः समागताः। तेभ्यस्तच्छ्रावयामास पुराणं वेदसंमितम्॥११८॥
verses.english: He knows that Narayana is the Supreme Soul, that He is the Supreme Lord, that He is Creator of Brahman himself. Narada recited this very ancient narrative which is perfectly consistent with the Vedas, to that assembly of Rishis crowned with ascetic success that came to the abode of Brahman. The gods Surya, having heard that narrative from those Rishis crowned with ascetic success, repeated it to the sixty-six thousands of Rishis, O king, of purified souls, that follow in his train.

verses.sanskrit: तेषां सकाशात्सूर्यस्तु श्रुत्वा वै भावितात्मनाम्। आत्मानुगामिनां राजन् श्रावयामास वै ततः॥११९॥
षट् षष्टिर्हि सहस्राणि ऋषीणां भावितात्मनाम्। सूर्यस्य तपतो लोकान् निर्मिता ये पुरः सराः॥१२०॥
verses.english: And the Sun, the deity that imparts heat to all the worlds, repeated that narrative to those Beings also, of purified souls, that have been created (by Brahman) for always travelling in the van of the Sun.

verses.sanskrit: तेषामकथयत्सूर्यः सर्वेषां भावितात्मनाम्। सूर्यानुगामिभिस्तात ऋषिभिस्तैर्महात्मभिः॥१२१॥
verses.english: The great Rishis who follow in the Sun's train, O son, repeated that excellent narrative to the deities assembled on the breast of Meru.

verses.sanskrit: मेरौ समागता देवाः श्राविताश्चेदमुत्तमम्। देवानां तु सकाशाद्वै ततः श्रुत्वासितो द्विजः॥१२२॥
श्रावयामास राजेन्द्र पितॄणां मुनिसत्तमः। मम चापि पिता तात कथयामास शान्तनुः॥१२३॥
verses.english: The best of ascetics, viz., the regener: Asita, then, having heard the narrative from the gods, repeated it to the Pitris, O king of kings.

verses.sanskrit: ततो मयाऽपि श्रुत्वा च कीर्तितं तव भारत। सुरैर्वा मुनिभिर्वापि पुराणं यैरिदं श्रुतम्॥१२४॥
verses.english: I heard it from my father Shantanu, O son, who recited it to me formerly. Myself having heard it from my father, I have repeated it to you, O Bharata.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वे ते परमात्मानं पूजयन्ते समन्ततः। इदमाख्यानमार्षेयं पारंपर्यागतं नृप॥१२५॥
verses.english: Gods and ascetics, they who have heard this excellent old narrative which is a Purana, all worship the Supreme Soul.

verses.sanskrit: नावासुदेवाभक्ताय त्वया देयं कथञ्चन। मत्तोऽन्यानि च ते राजन्नुपाख्यानशतानि वै॥१२६॥
verses.english: This discourse, belonging to the Rishis and thus handed down from one to another, should not, O king, be communicated by you to any one who is not a worshipper of Vasudeva.

verses.sanskrit: यानि श्रुतानि सर्वाणि तेषां सारोऽयमुद्धृतः। सुरासुरैर्यथा राजन्निर्मथ्यामृतमुद्धृतम्॥१२७॥
verses.english: This narrative, O king, is really the cream of the hundreds of other discourses that you have heard from me.

verses.sanskrit: एवमेतत्पुरा विप्रैः कथामृतमिहोद्धृतम्। यश्चेदं पठते नित्यं यश्चेदं शृणुयान्नरः॥१२८॥
verses.english: In days of yore, O king, the gods and the Asuras, in a body, churned the Ocean and raised the Ambrosia. Similarly the Brahmanas, in a body in days of yore, churned all the scriptures and raised this narrative, which resembles nectar.

verses.sanskrit: एकान्तभावोपगत एकान्तेषु समाहितः। प्राप्य श्वेतं महाद्वीपं भूत्वा चन्द्रप्रभो नरः॥१२९॥
verses.english: He who frequently reads this narrative, and he who frequently listens to it with rapt attention, in a secluded spot, and filled with devotion, succeeds, being possessed of lunar complexion, in living in the spacious insular continent known by the name of White Island. Forsooth, such a man succeeds in entering into Narayana of a thousand rays.

verses.sanskrit: स सहस्रार्चिषं देवं प्रविशेन्नात्र संशयः। मुच्येदार्तस्तथा रोगाच्छ्रुत्वेमामादितः कथाम्॥१३०॥
जिज्ञासुर्लभते कामान्भक्तो भक्तगतिं व्रजेत्। त्वयापि सततं राजन्नभ्यर्च्यः पुरुषोत्तमः॥१३१॥
verses.english: By listening to this narrative from the beginning, a sick person becomes freed from his disease. The man who simply desires to read or listen to this discourse, gets the fruition of all his wishes. By reading or listening to it. The devoted worshipper acquires the high end reserved for devoted worshippers.

verses.sanskrit: स हि माता पिता चैव कृत्स्नस्य जगतो गुरुः। ब्रह्मण्यदेवो भगवान्प्रीयतां ते सनातनः॥१३२॥
verses.english: You also, O king, should always adore and worship that foremost of all Beings. He is the father and the mother of all creatures, and He is an object of reverence to the entire universe.

verses.sanskrit:
युधिष्ठिर महाबाहो महाबुद्धिर्जनार्दनः।
              वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              श्रुत्वैतदाख्यानवरं धर्मराड्जनमेजय॥१३३॥
verses.english: Let the illustrious and Eternal God of the Brahmanas, Viz., Janarddana of great intelligence, be pleased with you, O Yudhisthira of mighty arms.

verses.sanskrit: भ्रातरश्चास्य ते सर्वे नारायणपराऽभवन्। जितं भगवता तेन पुरुषेणेति भारत॥१३४॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said Having listened to this best of discourses, O Janamejaya, king Yudhisthira the just, and all his brothers became devoted to Narayana.

verses.sanskrit: नित्यं जप्यपरा भूत्वा सरस्वतीमुदीरयन्। यो ह्यस्माकं गुरुश्रेष्ठः कृष्णद्वैपायनो मुनिः॥१३५॥
verses.english: And all of them, O Bharata, silently meditating upon Narayana (from that day), uttered these words for His glorification, viz., Victory to that holy and illustrious Being.

verses.sanskrit: जगौ परमकं जप्यं नारायणमुदीरयन्। गत्वाऽन्तरिक्षात्सततं क्षीरोदममृताशयम्॥१३६॥
verses.english: He, again, who is our best of preceptors, viz., the Island-born Krishna, devoted to penances, sung, uttering the word Narayana, that great Mantra which is worthy of being silently.

verses.sanskrit:
पूजयित्वा च देवेशं पुनरायात्स्वमाश्रमम्।
              भीष्म उवाच।
              एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं नारदोक्तं मयेरितम्॥१३७॥
verses.english: Passing through the sky to the Ocean of milk, which is always the abode of nectar, and adoring the great God there, be returned to his own hermitage.

verses.sanskrit: पारंपर्यागतं ह्येतत्पित्रा मे कथितं पुरा। सौतिरुवाच । एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं वैशम्पायनकीर्तितम्॥१३८॥
verses.english: Bhishma continued I have now recounted to you the discourse that was recited by Narada. That narrative has come down from person to person from very ancient times. I heard it from my father who formerly recounted it to me.

verses.sanskrit: जनमेजयेन तच्छ्रुत्वा कृतं सम्यग्यथाविधि। यूयं हि तप्ततपसः सर्वे च चरितव्रताः॥१३९॥
verses.english: Suta said I have now told you all that Vaishampayana recounted to Janamejaya. Having listened to Vaishampayana's narration, king Janamejaya severe duly satisfied all his duties according to the scriptural ordinances.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वे वेदविदो मुख्या नैमिषारण्यवासिनः। शौनकस्य महासत्रं प्राप्ताः सर्वे द्विजोत्तमाः॥१४०॥
verses.english: You have have all practised very penances and observed many high and excellent vows. Living in this sacred forest of Naimisha, you are foremost of all persons conversant with the Vedas.

verses.sanskrit: यजध्वं सुहुतैर्यज्ञैः शाश्वतं परमेश्वरम्। पारंपर्यागतं ह्येतत्पित्रा मे कथितं पुरा॥१४१॥
verses.english: You foremost of twice-born ones, you all have come to this great sacrifice of Shaunaka. Do you all worship that Eternal and Supreme Lord of the universe in excellent sacrifices, properly pouring libations of clarified butter to the fire with the help of Mantras and dedicating the same to Narayana. As for myself, I heard this excellent discourse which has come down from generation to generation, from my father who recited it to me formerly.
